items.title: Parse and preserve Authority runner provider declaration as host-neutral metadata
items.context: Read LATTICE_AUTHORITY_RUNNER_PROVIDER or equivalent runner config without constraining Authority identity to fake/codex/claude only. Known aliases may still map to execution adapters separately. Happy path: codex-cli or claude-code is accepted and emitted as runner/provider metadata. Edge: missing declaration preserves legacy behavior. Adversarial: custom declaration does not bypass API key, actor key, signature, lease, or server policy checks.
items.userSees: User sees "runnerProvider: codex-cli" and "runnerProviderValid: true" instead of "LATTICE_AUTHORITY_RUNNER_PROVIDER is invalid".

happy.desc: LATTICE_AUTHORITY_RUNNER_PROVIDER=codex-cli or antigravity normalizes to the same declaration string and is reported valid.

edge.desc: Missing runner provider still defaults to codex and claude / CLAUDE_CODE aliases still normalize to claude-code.

adversarial.desc: A custom provider declaration is not treated as authorization proof and does not set productionDone, receiptVerified, or authorityReady by itself.

verificationEvidence.note: TypeScript build passed after replacing closed Authority runner provider enum behavior with host-neutral declaration normalization.
Smoke proves default codex, claude/CLAUDE_CODE alias compatibility, and custom declarations such as codex-cli are valid locally.
Status/enforce-runner smokes prove custom declarations do not set productionDone, receiptVerified, or provider ownership locally.

items.title: Propagate provider declaration through register, heartbeat, SSE watch, claim, and takeover diagnostics
items.context: Ensure the same declaration used by the runner is visible to Authority calls and troubleshooting output, while signed claim remains the ownership boundary. Server rejection should be reported as server policy rejection, not as a local enum parse failure.
items.userSees: User sees "event: jobs.available" followed by a normal signed "claim_job" network event; there is no separate SSE-only ownership success path.

happy.desc: Declared provider metadata is sent consistently in actor key registration, runner registration, heartbeat, jobs.available SSE hint, and signed claim payloads.

edge.desc: authority_job_create accepts a non-enum provider string locally and leaves accept/reject to the server response.

adversarial.desc: SSE jobs.available stays a notification hint using the same routing semantics as POST claim; it never grants ownership without the normal signed claim accepted by the server.

verificationEvidence.note: Runner-client smoke proves custom codex-cli declarations propagate through actor key registration, runner registration, heartbeat, jobs.available diagnostics, and signed claim while the SSE hint remains non-owning.
Live job-loop smoke proves custom antigravity declarations propagate through live runner registration and signed claim while lease completion/release remains server-claim based.
Smokes prove authority_job_create accepts custom provider declarations in signed queue/delegated requests and dry-run diagnostics do not create ownership or bypass server policy.

items.title: Add focused regression tests for non-enum Authority provider declarations
items.context: Cover arbitrary provider declaration acceptance and propagation for Authority flows without expanding product scope or hardcoding a new exhaustive host list. Existing codex, claude, fake, and Antigravity-related behavior should remain compatible where those adapters are expected.
items.userSees: User sees "authority provider declaration smokes passed" after custom-provider, alias, SSE hint, and signed-claim boundary checks complete.

happy.desc: Focused smokes prove arbitrary provider declarations are accepted and propagated by CLI Authority flows.

edge.desc: Existing codex default, claude alias, and Antigravity-adjacent behavior remain compatible.

adversarial.desc: Regression tests prove declaration acceptance does not bypass credentials, signature, lease, or server-policy checks.

verificationEvidence.note: Build passed with regression tests updated for host-neutral provider declarations.
Focused smoke coverage proves arbitrary non-enum declarations are accepted locally while default codex and claude aliases remain compatible.
Focused live/runner smokes prove custom declarations propagate without bypassing credentials, signed claims, leases, SSE hint boundaries, or server policy.
